en.title: Health and the body
en.goal: Describe simple symptoms and body parts, and ask for basic medical help.
vocab: to not feel well / be unwell

phrases.t: I need to see a doctor.

dialogue.title: I'm not feeling well
lines: I don't feel well, my head hurts a lot.
Do you need to see a doctor?
Yes, is the hospital far from here?

teng.title: 疼 (téng) — describing pain
teng.body: To say a part of the body hurts, the structure in Chinese is very direct: Body part + 疼 (téng). 疼 itself means "to hurt", so no extra verb is needed: 头疼 = "head hurts".

teng-vs-bushufu.title: "Tóu téng" or "bù shūfu"?
teng-vs-bushufu.body: Téng (疼) describes a specific pain, in one part of the body. Bù shūfu (不舒服) is more general — feeling unwell without pointing to where it hurts. If you know exactly what hurts, use téng; if it's just a general feeling of "I feel bad", use bù shūfu.

le-change-of-state.title: 了 (le) marking a change of state
le-change-of-state.body: 了 at the end of the sentence (not right after the verb) shows that a new situation has begun or changed — as in "what's wrong?", a change noticed now that wasn't there before.

trueFalse.claim: This sentence is used when someone has a headache.
trueFalse.whyNote: Correct — 我头疼 (wǒ tóu téng) literally means "my head hurts", that is, a headache.
